claims: (1) S IS UNBOUNDED, UNCONDITIONALLY, A CLASSICAL PUBLISHED FACT. Verbatim from Conrey, 'A theory for the zeros of Riemann zeta and other L-functions (updated)' (arXiv:1407.4358), Section VIII 'The argument of the Riemann zeta-function': 'It is known that S(y) is unbounded, which implies that the logs in (154), which are Arg's, can accumulate. The roughest estimate is the known fact that S(y) = O(log y), which actually was not written explicitly in Riemann's paper, but only later by von Mangoldt.' The same section, verbatim: 'A celebrated theorem of Selberg [Selberg 1946a] states that S(y) over a large interval 0 < y < T satisfies a normal distribution with zero mean and variance S(y)^2-bar = (1/T) integral_0^T S(y)^2 dy = (1/(2 pi^2)) log log T + O(sqrt(log log T)).' The mean-square divergence (log log T -> infinity) gives limsup_{y -> infinity} |S(y)| = infinity UNCONDITIONALLY - the cleanest published derivation of the unboundedness statement.

(2) THE BEST PUBLISHED UPPER BOUND FOR S DIVERGES (UNDER RH). Carneiro, Chandee, Milinovich, 'Bounding S(t) and S_1(t) on the Riemann hypothesis' (arXiv:1309.1526; Mathematische Annalen 356 (2013) 939-968), Theorem 2, verbatim from ar5iv: 'Assume RH. For t sufficiently large, |S(t)| <= (1/4) . (log t)/(log log t) + O((log t log log log t)/(log log t)^2).' The paper's introduction, verbatim: 'This improves the previous bound of Goldston and Gonek, (1/2 + o(1)) . (log t)/(log log t), by a factor of 2.' Conrey's book (same section VIII), verbatim: 'Assuming the RH, the current best bound is given by [Carneiro et al. 2013] (see also [Goldston and Gonek 2007]) |S(y)| <= (1/4 + o(1)) log y / log log y for y -> infinity. It is important to bear in mind that these are upper bounds, and that S(y) may actually be much smaller.' Consequence for the program: NO published upper bound of finite constant exists at any heights range, and the best (RH) bound DIVERGES; unconditionally only the roughest S = O(log t) form (von Mangoldt) is the classic anchor.

(3) THE BEST PUBLISHED OMEGA FOR S (UNDER RH) GROWS LIKE (log t log log log t)/(log log t). Inoue, 'Large oscillations of the argument of the Riemann zeta-function' (arXiv:1904.11051), abstract verbatim: 'Let S(t) denote the argument of the Riemann zeta-function, defined as S(t) = (1/pi) Im log zeta(1/2 + it). Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we prove that S(t) = Omega_pm((log t log log log t)/(log log t)). This improves the classical Omega-results of Montgomery [14, Theorem 2] and matches with the Omega-result obtained by Bondarenko and Seip [1, Theorem 2].' Combined with (2): under RH the published picture is (1/4 + o(1)) log/loglog >= |S| >= (1 - o(1)) log log log / loglog in order - a BAND OF OSCILLATION THAT OPENS AS LOG LOG LOG T.

(4) SHORT-INTERVAL DELTA-OMEGAS. (a) UNCONDITIONAL: Tsang, 'Some Omega-theorems for the Riemann zeta-function', Acta Arith. 46 (1986) 369-395, as cited in Inoue (arXiv:2510.14309): 'Later, Tsang gave a proof of this result in [13] and also proved that [1.3] holds with eta = 1/3 unconditionally' where (1.3) is sup_{t in [T,2T]} { +/-(S(t+h) - S(t)) } >= c (h log T)^{1/3} for large T and h in [a (log T)^{-1}, b (log log T)^{-1}]. (b) UNDER RH: Inoue, 'Explicit extreme values of the argument of the Riemann zeta-function' (arXiv:2510.14309), Theorem 1, verbatim: 'Assume RH. For any large T and any h in [C/log T, c/log log T] with positive constants C large and c small, we have sup_{T <= t <= 2T} { +/- (S(t+h) - S(t)) } >= (1 - E) sqrt((h/pi) log T),' with the error E -> 0 (improving the earlier constant sqrt(2/(e pi)) < 1 from the Selberg-Tsang-Inoue approach). Consequence: the oscillation of S is published at every intermediate scale between point-omega and full-range omega, unconditionally and under RH.

(5) THE E19 GAP STAYS EXACTLY AS RECORDED (NO NEW PUBLISHED AT-ZEROS OMEGA FOUND). This audit pulled the current primary literature on S (2013, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2023, 2025 sources; Conrey's updated book; the Selberg CLT normalization line 2407.14867 / 2505.23573 / 2511.18275 already in the E19 record) and found NO published theorem stating limsup_{gamma -> infinity (zeros)} |S(gamma)| = infinity (no at-zeros Omega theorem of any order appeared in the sources pulled). The crude gap-transfer (general-t Omega + zero density / spacing heuristics -> at-zeros Omega) is, as E19 established, not a valid crude argument. So the formal state of the absolute clause G-hs1 / A1 (uniform finite |S(zero)| <= K, data-free, at the zeros) is precisely: NOT A LIVE PUBLISHED THEOREM (no published theorem supplies it - F1, now re-confirmed against 2025-grade sources) AND NOT YET REFUTED BY PUBLISHED ANALYSIS (no published at-zeros Omega; E19). Under the published RH picture (2)+(3) the clause is INCOMPATIBLE with S's proven oscillation except possibly exactly at the zero ordinates - i.e., the clause would require S to vanish in growth at exactly the zero set, which no published source states or suggests. Status label: UNDER PRESSURE - not refuted - unchanged, now with the full 2025 citation record.

(6) VERDICT FOR THE FACE (NO MOVEMENT). The analytic closure routes for the terminal face, against now fully cited primary sources: (i) UNIFORM ABSOLUTE CLAUSE (G-hs1/A1): DEAD as a published input - no published theorem, published upper bounds all diverge; (ii) QUANTITATIVE GROWTH ROUTE (the 4/7 door of the Levinson/PRZZ (1.2) machinery, 0310-0312): ALIVE, PINNED at 4/7 - the only analytic path, unchanged by this audit; (iii) THETA = INFINITY CONJECTURE LANE (ThetaInf module, 0290): ALIVE, CONJECTURAL BY NATURE - Bettin-Gonek Theorem 1 (cited in ThetaInf): for FIXED theta > 0, the antecedent I_N(0,T) <<_epsilon T^{1+epsilon} for 2 <= N <= T^theta implies zeta zero-free in |sigma - 1/2| > 1/(2 theta), so the theta = infinity conjecture implies RH - it is a CONJECTURE (Farmer), not a proven theorem, and no 2025-grade source in this audit proved it or a sufficient fragment past 4/7. The wall {theta | 4/7 < theta} is UNMOVED. The terminal face at tCE44 (210,278 above H0, 0349) remains OPEN. NO RH CLAIM.
